A Matrix protocol mechanism that allows.message: A Matrix protocol mechanism that allows Waldur to register as a service on the homeserver. The homeserver pushes events to Waldur via a webhook, and Waldur can create rooms, invite users, and send messages on behalf of a bot user.

Two shared secrets generated during setu.message: Two shared secrets generated during setup. The AS token authenticates Waldur when calling the homeserver API. The HS token authenticates the homeserver when sending events to Waldur via webhook.

A configuration file that must be added.message: A configuration file that must be added to the Matrix homeserver to register Waldur as an appservice. Contains tokens, bot user ID, webhook URL, and namespace declarations.

A human-readable room address (e.g., #wa.message: A human-readable room address (e.g., #waldur-a1b2c3d4:matrix.example.com). Waldur generates aliases based on the project UUID.

Matrix permission system. Project owners.message: Matrix permission system. Project owners and admins get elevated power levels (50+), allowing them to manage the room. Regular members get the default level (0).

A snapshot of all messages in a room, sa.message: A snapshot of all messages in a room, saved as a JSON file. Optionally includes media files in a ZIP archive. Can be triggered manually, on a schedule, or automatically before project deletion.

Matrix is an open protocol for decentral.message: Matrix is an open protocol for decentralized communication. This integration registers Waldur as a Matrix appservice, enabling automatic creation of project chat rooms, member synchronization based on project roles, bot commands for operational queries, and chat history exports for compliance.

The setup process generates authenticati.message: The setup process generates authentication tokens and a registration YAML that must be added to your Matrix homeserver configuration.

Click \"Setup appservice\" and optionall.message: Click "Setup appservice" and optionally provide the Waldur URL reachable by the homeserver

Copy the generated registration YAML to.message: Copy the generated registration YAML to your homeserver configuration directory

Register the YAML file in your homeserve.message: Register the YAML file in your homeserver settings (e.g., app_service_config_files in Synapse, or the equivalent for your homeserver)

Restart the homeserver — it will begin s.message: Restart the homeserver — it will begin sending events to the Waldur webhook

Each project can have one chat room. Roo.message: Each project can have one chat room. Rooms are created by project owners and automatically populated with project members. Owners can disable a room (kicking all members and exporting history) and later re-enable it or delete it entirely.

The homeserver pushes room events to Wal.message: The homeserver pushes room events to Waldur via the appservice webhook. Waldur processes bot commands and ignores other events.

The Waldur bot responds to commands post.message: The Waldur bot responds to commands posted in project chat rooms. Type a command in the room and the bot will reply with the relevant information.

Chat history can be exported as JSON fil.message: Chat history can be exported as JSON files with optional media attachments. Exports can be triggered manually, run on a daily schedule, or happen automatically when a room is disabled or a project is deleted.
